intro_html: A good chicken curry is warm, fragrant, and endlessly forgiving, which makes it perfect for meal prep. This one packs in the protein, keeps the fat low, and stays cheap per serving thanks to a few pantry staples. One batch makes 14 servings.
cost_closing_html: About $3.40 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings comes in around 59g protein for about 568 calories, at roughly $2.03 a bowl.
upsell_html: Fragrant, filling, and easy on the budget, this curry is meal prep you will actually crave. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: A single jar of curry powder carries the whole flavor and stretches across many future batches.
Greek yogurt stands in for coconut milk or cream and keeps this bowl light and cheap.
Whole carrots bought by the pound cost far less than the pre-cut bags and stretch the meal further.
make_it: Add the chicken breast, chopped onion, sliced carrots, and minced garlic to the crock.
Stir in the curry powder and pour in the chicken broth.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken is tender.
Shred the chicken, then stir in the Greek yogurt for creaminess.
Whisk the cornstarch with a little water and stir it in to thicken the sauce.

head.description: A high-protein Indian meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 568 calories and 59 grams of protein for roughly $3.40 each (at everyday cost).
